doc.title: Byron Stripling interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 25, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]

chapter: Count Basie band and Thad Jones
title: Thad Jones's death
summary: Stripling recalls hearing of Thad's death at the Village Vanguard and his first experience of grief.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: I like your impressions of him conducting. He had a certain, I mean, nobody conducted like him.

Well when you talk to some other people about that, ask them how his conducting inspired them, I think you’ll get the same response, really a way of giving you some energy and that kind of thing. So then he went back to Europe. I remember talking to him a couple of times on the phone. And then I’ll never forget I went to the Village Vanguard one Monday night and I walked in and they have a picture of him on the thing conducting. And I paid my admission and I looked at that picture and I said that’s my man, Thad. And I walked over and I think I saw somebody from the band and I said, “Did you know that Thad passed away today?” He says, “You’re kidding.” And I remember for me that was my first experience with somebody I loved dying. That was the first time I cried you know. Because I was very confused. You know you don’t know when you first experience death, and we all experience it more as we get older, but this is a guy that I’d given big hugs to all the time, and sitting by him on the bus and trying to © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-

talk to him about music and what I should practice and he would help me when I was improvising, and things like that, and supported me in my life, and I just developed a love for him. And then all of a sudden somebody said well he’s dead. So that was my first one with that, and I was just trying to deal with, well how do you deal with when somebody dies? But then you have to look back and say God I’m so thankful that I was able to sit by this guy who I love and was such a great inspiration, and it’s a great memory for me.
Really and the Vanguard orchestra, I mean it was an inspiration to so many players coming up and writers. That was great stuff.
